A reminder can be asked to keep one eye on you. There are two ways one gets away — it rings and you never answer it, or its moment comes while a fence is shut and there is none left for it to ring at — and one switch for both, since nobody knows in advance which way it will be. Either way you get one quiet word about it: no sound, no screen, once. The switch is on each reminder, under «what happens»; these are what it means by «later».
And this is the whole wait when the reminder has nothing left to ring: a date that has been, a countdown that ran out. Nothing else is coming, so there is no hurry.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_3_0
string-array.item: A reminder takes the whole screen only when nothing else is open: with an app in front of you it arrives as a banner instead, and the banner opens it.
Putting one off: ten minutes, two hours, tomorrow at the same time, the weekend (Friday at 20:30, or whenever you say in Settings) and next week — as buttons a thumb cannot miss.
A reminder no longer needs a trigger or an action. Text and a tag is enough: it is simply kept, under "kept, not timed".
With more than one trigger you choose between "any of them" and "all of them" — all of them rings with the last to happen, and the card ticks off the ones already behind you.
The editor reads as four parts, each in its own card with its own icon, and every edge you can press is finally visible.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_3_1
string-array.item: While a reminder has no "when" yet, the three answers people give most — in half an hour, tonight, tomorrow morning — are one tap away, before "Add a trigger".
Swiping a card answers the moment it takes: the glyph springs and the colour deepens, on the same tick as the vibration.

For a screen reader: sections are headings, day and action toggles say whether they are on, every trigger says its kind, and Done and Delete are actions on the card itself — a swipe is not something TalkBack can do.
Empty screens have a face: an icon before the sentence.
Done times follow the phone\'s 12/24-hour setting, the time wheels grow with a large font size, and the small grey notes in the editor are readable on the light theme too.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_3_2
string-array.item: "On" finally looks on. A chosen tag, action, preset or segment swaps ink and paper — the same inversion as the Save button — instead of turning a slightly lighter grey.
A chosen day is a solid disc in the time colour, so a week reads as a pattern of lit and unlit.
In the editor, each trigger row wears its family\'s colour: a date is blue, a place green, a chance violet, before a word is read.
The editor\'s cards stand off the ground the way Home\'s do, and toggles turn over with a short fade rather than popping.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_4_0
string-array.item: Rwilco now keeps its own eye on your places, next to the phone\'s: it reads where you are, judges each place for itself, and decides how long it can look away — an hour standing still across town, two minutes walking up to a door. GPS only near a place and moving, so the battery hardly notices.
Settings → Location says what that watch last saw and when it looks next.
Settings → Places keeps places by name — home, work, the gym — and the place sheet offers them whole: name, pin and radius in one tap.
A place seen by both the phone and the watch rings once.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_4_2
string-array.item: Pausing a reminder now says what it will do — the word "Pause" or "Resume" next to the button, because a pause glyph on its own reads as "this is paused" just as easily.
It is bigger, it sits up with the reminder\'s own words instead of among the small grey glyphs that cannot be pressed, and it takes a finger that stays. Let go early and nothing happens.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_7
string-array.item: A repeating reminder now says so on its card. One whose whole arrangement is “cada 6 h” carries no trigger at all, so its card said nothing whatsoever about when it rings — it now shows the shape and, under it, the part that is easy to get wrong: the clock starts when you mark it done, not when it rang.

And taking a “hecho” back really does put things where they were. The reminder came back correctly, but the alarm stayed set for the round you had just undone — and then refused to ring, because the row no longer agreed with it.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_6
string-array.item: “Hecho” now means the same thing wherever you say it. Swiping a card done on Home went straight to the done list, even for a reminder you had asked to repeat — so a routine like “cada 1 h” was finished by the swipe instead of starting its next round. It now reactivates itself and counts the next one from your “hecho”, exactly as the notification always did.
On the alert screen, “Hecho” is the button at the bottom. “Ver” used to sit below it, which is where a half-awake thumb lands — so answering an alarm could hand you the edit form instead.

And saving that form no longer brings a moment back from the dead. A repeating reminder that had rung and was waiting for you came back from the editor as “lo siguiente”, three quarters of an hour in the past, with an alarm set for a moment already gone.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_5
string-array.item: A reminder that repeats no longer rings on and on. “Cada 6 h” counts from the moment you deal with it, so one you had not answered kept handing back the same moment, and an alarm already in the past arrives at once — over and over until you tapped Hecho. It rang once, waits on Home as overdue, and comes back six hours after you say so.
Editing one no longer resets it. Fixing a typo used to throw away the moment its recurrence counts from, which either stopped the reminder dead or hurled its next one back to the day it was written.
Asking for a recurrence now sets the alarm there and then. On a reminder with no other “when”, it was the one change nothing noticed, and the alarm waited for the next restart.
Arriving somewhere no longer swallows an appointment. “Al llegar a casa, o mañana a las nueve” recorded the arrival against tomorrow’s nine o’clock, and tomorrow passed in silence.
Changing what hour the day starts at now moves the reminders that depend on it, instead of waiting for a reboot.
The place watch ignores a reading too old to speak for where the phone is now, rather than believing this morning’s and then dismissing a real arrival as somewhere it thought you already were.
The notification action wears two stacked banners instead of a bell: a bell was saying “an alarm”, which is every one of the four.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_4
string-array.item: The chips that reuse a text or a tag work again. Giving them a second thing to do on a held finger had quietly taken the first one away: two gesture handlers on one chip, and the tap went to neither. Tap uses it, hold still mends the list.
Those rows now stop at five and put the rest behind a “…” with a search box, instead of growing into a wall to read past on the way to the keyboard.

The “when” shortcuts are yours now: the lengths, hours and places you actually set, most used first, re-hung on today. Until there is a history they are the three everybody starts with. Settings can also sort the six kinds by what you use, under “Most used”.
Adding a tag no longer asks the same question twice — its own + is the answer to that field, and Save steps aside until you are done with it.
Times in Settings sit in the middle of their frame instead of up against the top of it.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_3
string-array.item: Nothing rings twice on its own. A moment that has rung is spent: a timer you have not got round to waits on Home as overdue, as it should, but it no longer goes off again by itself — not from a stray alarm, not after a reboot, not from the six-hourly safety net.

Arriving where you already are is not arriving. "When I get home", written on the sofa, now waits until it has seen you leave, and waits cheaply: half an hour between looks and no GPS, because the only thing that can happen indoors is going out.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_2
string-array.item: Swiping a card no longer acts on the swipe alone. Open it and hold it there: the glyph fills like a glass of water, and at half a second it takes. Let go, or slide back, and nothing has happened — so a card can no longer be dealt with on the way past while you scroll.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_1
string-array.item: Fixed a reminder that could pause itself with nobody touching the phone: a finger still on the pause button when the app lost the screen left the hold armed, and it finished itself off the moment you came back. A press that survives the app leaving the screen is no longer a press.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_7_0
string-array.item: Recurrence grew up. "Comes back" is a card of its own, with the answers people give most as buttons — the next day, every 6 h, every week — the whole list behind the dots, and "Custom" to build one from parts.

Most of them count from YOU, not from the clock: "every 6 h" means six hours after you mark it done, which is how medicine actually works. There is also "the nth weekday of each month" for the ones that are a date rather than a habit.
Any recurrence you build can be kept under a name from the same pane, and then it is a button too — most used first, editable and deletable from the list.
Settings says what "the next day" means: the hour a recurrence in days, weeks or months lands on. Never earlier, so something dealt with at midnight comes back in the morning.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_6_1
string-array.item: A countdown is a length of time now, not a date. It used to be stored as the moment it worked out to, which is why a preset could not really hold one: it would have kept the half hour after the day you wrote it.
So "in half an hour" in a preset now means half an hour from whenever you use it — a real timer, every time, in one tap.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_6_0
string-array.item: Preset buttons under the date, where the app\'s own name used to be. One tap writes the reminder — no form. If the preset has no words of its own it asks for them and nothing else, with the keyboard already up. Most used first, scrollable when there are many, and the "+" at the end says which presets get a button.
The glowing card can be swiped now, like every other one.
It also says when it is showing a postponement — "Pospuesto hasta" rather than "Lo siguiente" — so a reminder you pushed away is not a countdown you cannot explain.
Fixed: undoing a swipe could hand the card back frozen halfway across the screen. It was also acting on the swipe more than once, which is why undo sometimes gave you back something already done.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_5_2
string-array.item: A preset\'s name is now just its label. What a reminder made from it SAYS is a separate, optional line — "words it starts with".

Leave that empty and the preset is a shape waiting for words: picking it opens the reminder with the field empty, the cursor in it and the keyboard already up. Fill it in and the reminder arrives written, with nothing to do but save.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_5_1
string-array.item: Fixed: a reminder you had dealt with could ring again. "Done" now finishes a reminder, full stop — a place reminder marked done in the morning no longer goes off on the way back through the same door.

Repeating is something you ask for: a "Keep reminding me" switch under the triggers, off unless you turn it on. Choosing "a time that repeats" or "at random" turns it on for you, in plain sight, and you can turn it back off.
Your existing reminders keep the behaviour that matched their trigger: repeating times and random ones carry on repeating, places and dates now finish when you deal with them.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_5_0
string-array.item: Presets: a reminder you make often, kept by name. Write one as usual and turn on "Keep as a preset" — the words become its name, and the tags, the when and the what happens are kept with it.

Once you have one, "New" asks first: blank, or from a preset. The presets come up as big buttons, the ones you actually use at the top, each with a colour of its own so your hand finds it without reading.
Tapping one opens the form already filled in, so a date that has since passed gets seen and fixed rather than silently written.
Settings says what a blank reminder starts with — full screen, notification, sound, vibration — for anyone who never wants a sound, or always wants the screen.
Settings is quieter: the theme is three small icons, and the paragraphs of explanation are folded behind a (?) beside each title.

Hold one of the "or reuse one" chips — a phrase or a tag — and the list opens to be mended: rename one and it is renamed on every reminder that carries it; drop a phrase and it stops being offered, without touching what you wrote.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_4_3
string-array.item: Holding that button now dims the whole screen and fills one ring in the middle of it — where no thumb ever is — with the icon and the word inside. And it takes 700ms rather than two seconds: long enough to mean it, short enough not to feel like a punishment.
The word under the button is small now, so a reminder\'s own words get the width back.

string-array.item: The place watch, put through simulated journeys and a night on the bedside table: it now looks again within a quarter of an hour when it cannot yet tell how fast you are going (an hour blind is ninety motorway kilometres), remembers your speed across its longest waits, and only wakes the GPS for a phone it knows is moving.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_8_0
string-array.item: The place watch now spends a great deal less battery. It knows how far away a place is — nothing 300 km off can be arrived at for two and a half hours, so it stops asking — and it asks the phone\'s own motion sensor whether anything moved at all, which is free, and skips the reading entirely when nothing did.

Sitting inside a place you have a «when I leave» rule for used to be the most expensive thing the app did. It now starts at half an hour and speeds up only as you actually cross the place — and the moment you really do walk out, the motion sensor pulls the next look forward.
Below half a battery every wait stretches, gently at first and then quickly, until at a quarter left it is one look an hour and no GPS at all.
A full-screen alarm nobody answered used to hold the screen on until somebody came home. It now lets go when the ringing does.

Settings has the whole account of it: every look the watch took and the numbers it decided the next one from, and an optional quiet notice if it ever reads your location more than twenty times in an hour.

resources.string: Only when I cross the line
A question in the shade when you cross the line, with «yes, just now» one tap away.
Crossing the line is the deed itself — leaving the garage is the car moving. The count starts again by itself, and a quiet notice offers to undo it.
Being there is enough: if you are already there when everything else is due, it rings.
Being away is enough: if you are already away when everything else is due, it rings.
It has to see you arrive. If you are already there, it waits until you leave and come back.
It has to see you leave. If you are already away, it waits until you go there and leave again.
It does not ring at the line, but once you have been there that long.
It does not ring at the line, but once you have been away that long.
The phone checks a few times over that stretch. Stepping out for a moment is fine; leaving for good is not, and then it waits for you to arrive again.
Only counts when the phone is there — or when it is not. Pick from the places you keep in Settings.
No place kept by name yet. Make one here; it is kept in Settings → Places.

This can never ring: it asks to be in two places that cannot both be true at once.
Under «all» this one stops the whole reminder: it can never happen, so the set never completes and nothing ever rings.
«All» rings with the last of them to happen, in any order and however far apart. If you meant «when I get here, and only in the evening», put the hours on this one with «and only if».
On its own it rings when the range opens — at 17:00, for «from 17:00 to 19:00».
With «at once» this is the stretch the others have to fall inside: «at the office, between five and seven».
All of them true at the same moment; rings the instant the last one becomes true.
Two moments cannot be the same moment, so «at once» never rings here. Leave one moment and make the rest time ranges, or places you only have to be at («while I\'m at…», not «when I leave»).

string-array.name: whats_new_0_9_0
string-array.item: A new kind of trigger: a time range. «From 17:00 to 19:00» — on its own it rings when the range opens, and it is what the two below are worth writing for.
«And only if» can now be a place as well as an hour: «at nine, and only if I am at home», or only if you are not. Pick from the places you keep in Settings.

And a third way to read several triggers: «at once». All of them true at the same moment — «at the office, between five and seven» rings when you arrive if it is already five, and at five if you are already there.

The editor now says when a set of triggers can never ring, instead of letting you find out in a week: hours that never meet the moments they restrict, two places that cannot both be true, two moments asked to be the same moment. Under «all», it says which one is stopping the whole reminder.

Fewer location reads again. Where you are is now the last thing checked and the first thing skipped: the hours are settled before a position is read at all, and a place is left completely alone while the hours its reminder needs cannot hold — nothing is spent watching the office at three in the morning for something that can only ring at five.

resources.string: How a reminder buzzes when it rings. Separate from the touch feedback above: this is the alarm, not the interface. Some phones have one strength and nothing else, and on those «gentle» feels the same as «strong».
A reminder never buzzes for more than a minute: a vibration motor is a coil driving a weight, and both get hot. An alarm that has buzzed for a minute has made its point anyway.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_10_0
string-array.item: Tags carry a colour now, worked out from the word itself — nothing to choose and nothing stored, so the same tag is the same colour on every screen and after a reinstall. The palette stays well clear of the amber that means «next» and of the three trigger colours, so a tag can never read as a place or as the thing about to ring.

Two chips at the end of the row: «sin etiqueta» for the reminders nobody has filed, and «en pausa» for the ones quietly switched off. Both appear only while they have something in them, so the row does not end in two chips you can never act on.
The vibration is yours to choose: strong or gentle, in pulses or unbroken — with a button that plays it, because a vibration is the one thing here nobody can look at.

And it can no longer run away. A reminder\'s buzz used to repeat until the app stopped it, which meant that an app that died mid-alarm left the motor running until somebody rebooted. The whole minute is now handed to the system up front, so it ends whatever happens — and even the unbroken rhythm lets the motor go for a moment between stretches.

resources.string: What a reminder sounds like. The four of ours are made the way a car makes one — a low tone struck and left to ring, then quiet — rather than a beep in the band that makes a sound shrill. They are quieter than the phone\'s alarm tone on purpose; tap one to hear it.
A different sound when it keeps asking
A tone you hear once and a tone you hear five times are not the same choice. Off, both use the sound above.
For «sound until answered»: how many times in all, counting the first, and how far apart. It stops the moment the reminder is dealt with, snoozed or paused.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_11_0
string-array.item: Four sounds of our own, and they are the point of this one: two or three short tones in the band the ear notices most, and then silence — the way a car tells you something rather than the way an alarm clock does. They are in Settings, and they play when you tap them. Your alarms keep the phone\'s own tone until you pick one, on purpose: these are quieter, and an alarm nobody recognises is an alarm somebody sleeps through.
Any file works too — mp3, wav, whatever the phone can open.

«Sound» is now two tiles: once, or until answered. The insistent one comes back every few minutes until you deal with the reminder — five times, five minutes apart, both yours to change — and stops the moment you answer it, snooze it or pause it.

resources.string: The last five releases. You are on %1$s.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_11_1
string-array.item: This, at the bottom of Settings: the last five releases, whenever you want them rather than only once after an update.

The time range trigger has an icon that means a range — a clock with a slice of it filled. It was an hourglass, which says «time passing» and said it in nearly the same glyph as the countdown two tiles away.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_11_2
string-array.item: A reminder the phone slept through no longer costs you the next one. Catching up on a missed moment was recording the ring against the moment the re-arm had already moved on to, so a daily reminder skipped a day after every night the phone was off, and a set of rules lost whichever moment came next. Fixed, with a test that would have caught it.

The place watch keeps its chain of looks whatever happens to one of them: a look that runs out of time or fails leaves the next one armed, and the next look is armed before anything rings rather than after. Its three doors — the alarm, a geofence, the app starting up — now take turns instead of writing over each other, which is what was costing an extra fix five seconds after the one just taken whenever its own alarm woke the app.
Granting «all the time» in Settings arms your place reminders the moment you come back, not up to six hours later. Allowing exact alarms does the same for the rest.

The app stopped checking GitHub for updates every time the place watch woke it up — a few dozen times a day, for a file that had not changed. Opening the app checks, as before, and so does the twelve-hourly check.

A reminder that comes back «every 6 h» and has rung once without an answer stays overdue until you deal with it: it no longer rings again at the hour of the trigger that only ever meant the first time.
«Done» on the notification of a reminder you had already deleted takes the notification down.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_11_3
string-array.item: A place that is only ever asked about — «at nine, and only if I am home», or a place under «all at once» that cannot ring on its own — is now watched only in the five minutes before that moment, and not all day. And once a reminder is coming back on its own schedule («every 6 h»), nothing of its places is watched or geofenced any more: the recurrence is in charge, and arriving somewhere does not ring it.
«All at once» sets are now scheduled from the whole set: «at nine, and between eight and ten on Mondays» arms Monday at nine, not tomorrow at nine. Its cards on Home say the same.

A full-screen reminder that arrives as a banner — an app in front, or usage access never granted — now makes its sound and its buzz. It used to be silent, because the sound was left to a screen that never came. Likewise every «until answered» repeat of a full-screen reminder.
«Sound» or «vibration» with the notification unticked no longer does nothing: whatever you asked for is carried by a notification, because that is how the phone makes it.
Under «all of them», a phone off across two of its moments no longer waits for ever for the second one: both are owed when it wakes, and the last one rings.

Editing a reminder\'s rules — deleting one, moving a place — no longer hands one circle another\'s memory, which could ring «arriving home» at somebody sitting at home. A first fix too sloppy to place you is read on the side that rings nothing, and «only if I am home» judged on such a fix holds rather than saying no.
The alert screen names the rule that actually rang, not the first one on the list.
Home no longer comes back from the background built for an hour that has passed; the first swipe after every alert works; the pin panel scrolls; a tag filter survives the tag changing its spelling.

The place sheet: a rotation while it was locating or searching no longer leaves it busy for ever, and the radius slider lands on the tick it shows. A countdown can no longer be set past a week and then refuse to save without a word. After eleven at night the date-time sheet offers tomorrow. A place condition being edited keeps its own place even if the saved one was renamed or deleted. Editing a built-in recurrence preset saves the edit. Saving a reminder that rang and was dealt with while the editor was open keeps the «done».
Settings: «approximate» location says what is actually missing (the precise grant) instead of sending you round the background one; a look the watch has not yet taken says «ago», not «in».

string-array.name: whats_new_0_11_4
string-array.item: What a recurrence means for a place, put right. «When I get home, every day»: dealt with, the reminder rests until the span is up (tomorrow at your day\'s start hour), and then the place is armed again — and it rings on the next arrival, not at nine. The nine o\'clock never rings by itself when a place is waiting; 0.11.3 had stopped watching the place altogether, which was wrong.

A place that has rung is owed a leaving before it rings again. Neither a fix inside nor the phone\'s own geofence re-reading the line counts: the app has to have seen you outside since. To see that, the phone\'s geofences now report leavings as well as arrivals; a leaving is written down and never rings unless the rule is about leaving.
«At eight, and then every six hours» is unchanged: once a date has been, the recurrence\'s own moment is the ring.

When two full-screen reminders ring within moments of each other: one after the other — the next appears the instant you answer the first — or all at once, the screen split into a strip per reminder. Each keeps its own notification either way.
One of the snooze buttons is a length you choose. Ten minutes and two hours are always there beside it.
Rings in ten seconds through the real path — lock the phone to see the full screen. Pick what to try: only the sound, only the buzz, the lot.
A notification has room for three buttons and "Done" is one, so it carries two snoozes. The full-screen alert offers all of them.
A reminder notification channel is muted on the phone, so those reminders arrive silently or not at all.
The alarm volume is at zero, so a reminder with sound plays nothing.
Do Not Disturb is on total silence right now. Reminders only get through it if Rwilco is allowed to.
Alarms already get through every other Do Not Disturb mode; total silence needs Rwilco to be allowed through, and that can only be granted in advance.
Background use is restricted for Rwilco, so nothing re-arms reminders while it is closed.
Battery optimisation can stop Rwilco in the background. The alarms still ring; the net that re-arms them may not run.
This phone has no such settings page; the app\'s own page opened instead.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_12_0
string-array.item: Your reminders can now live somewhere other than this phone. In Settings, «Backup»: an encrypted copy of everything — reminders, presets, places — in a private GitHub repository of yours, refreshed a quarter of an hour after any change. It is sealed with a passphrase of yours before it leaves the phone, so GitHub sees a file and its size and never a word of what is in it; every copy is a commit, so the repository\'s history is the copy\'s history. Off by default, and the app works exactly as before without it. Lose the passphrase and the copy is a locked box: nobody can open it, this app included.

Two reminders ringing at the same moment both reach you now. The second one used to take the screen from the first, whose notification then sat silently in the shade — indistinguishable from never having rung. Now they queue: one after the other, with the next appearing the instant you answer, or side by side as strips, one «Hecho» each. It is a choice, in Settings › Alerts.

«Al llegar al curro, a partir de las siete» no longer counts down to tomorrow. When hours sit beside a place under «a la vez», they are the place\'s hours and not a moment of their own, so Home says what actually rings: the arrival.

And a sweep over everything between a reminder\'s moment and you noticing it. Do Not Disturb no longer swallows a full-screen reminder: they are alarms to the phone now, not chats. A reminder that the system refuses to show full-screen makes its noise as a notification instead of arriving silently. The sound asks the phone for the speaker, so a podcast cannot bury it, and the buzz is an alarm\'s buzz, which the silent switch keeps. A moment the phone slept through by a couple of minutes rings like the moment itself instead of arriving as a grey note. And every way a firing had of quietly deciding not to ring now re-arms itself first.

Settings says out loud the five things the phone does to keep reminders from you and nobody ever finds: battery optimisation, restricted background use, total-silence Do Not Disturb, the alarm volume at zero, and a notification channel muted by hand.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_13_0
string-array.item: The encrypted copy is yours to pace now. In Settings › Backup, «how often»: every hour, every four (the new normal), every eight, daily, every three days or weekly — and it counts the way anacron does, from the last copy that actually worked. A copy that fails is retried until it goes through, and only then does the wait start again: three days failing, a copy on the fourth and «every week» puts the next one on the eleventh day. There is also «only over wifi», and the screen says what the last copy weighed, so the data it costs is a number you can see.

A small red circle in the corner of the main screen counts what is waiting to be copied. Tap it and the copy happens on the spot: the number turns into a ring while it goes up and a tick when it lands, and then it goes away. No copy waiting, no circle.

Before handing the app a token you can now check it: «Test the repository and the token» says whether it exists, whether it is private, whether the token can write and whether there is already a copy in it — without writing a byte. And «Test a file» opens a copy, tells you what is in it and changes nothing: a rehearsal of a restore.
The passphrase field has a bar under it, so you can see when it is long enough instead of guessing: at least twelve characters with letters and digits in them.
Updates can wait for wifi too (Settings › Updates). The app is fifty megabytes and an update downloads all of it. «Check now» still goes over whatever there is, because you asked for it.

Opening a running countdown no longer restarts it. The sheet always handed back a fresh timer, so «in ten minutes» quietly became ten minutes from whenever you pressed save — which is also why a reminder would sometimes drop out of the big card at the top after an edit. A length you actually change is still a new timer.
The permission request 0.12.0 added on launch now comes after the first screen rather than on top of it, and asks once instead of on every rotation.

resources.string: It plays %1$d times in all. Here the waits are shortened; the real one is every %2$d min, and it stops the moment you deal with the reminder.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_14_0
string-array.item: The four chimes are rebuilt, and they are softer. They used to be beeps in the band that makes any sound feel shrill (up to 1568 Hz, with flat-topped envelopes); now they are low notes — 330 to 800 Hz — struck and left to decay like a bar hit with a mallet, each carrying its own octave underneath for warmth and almost nothing above it. The idea is the chime a car plays when you leave a door open, not the buzzer: «Puerta abierta» is exactly that, one soft tone struck four times, unhurried. They are still the app\'s own, still synthesised by a script in the repository, and still licensed by nobody.

The insistent sound can be heard before you trust it: «Oír la tanda insistente» plays the whole round — as many times as it would really come back — with the waits shortened to something you will sit through, and says what the real wait is underneath.

resources.string: What the app has been doing, to copy and send when something breaks.

A week of decisions, and the state everything is judged from. It holds no reminder text, no tag or place names and no token — a bug lives in the moments, not in the words. Copy it and paste it wherever you are asking for help.
What it says about the last week goes with it.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_15_0
string-array.item: There is a «Diagnostics» screen at the very bottom of Settings now. It holds a week of what the app actually did — every firing that rang and every one it decided not to, the re-arms, what the phone was allowing at the time — plus the state each reminder is judged by: what it is armed for, when it last rang, what it is waiting on. One button copies the lot, so when something does not ring you can paste it wherever you are asking for help instead of describing it from memory. It deliberately holds no reminder text, no tag or place names and no token: a bug lives in the moments, not in the words, and places are rounded to about a kilometre.

A reminder with more than one trigger now shows where each one stands, on the card. Under «todos», a tick for the ones that have already happened and a hollow circle for what it is still waiting on. Under «a la vez», a filled dot for the ones that are true at this moment — you are inside that place, the hour is inside that window — and a hollow one for the rest, changing back on its own the moment one stops holding. It is the difference between those two words, which until now happened somewhere nobody could see.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_15_1
string-array.item: The diagnostics screen keeps up with itself. It built its report once, when it opened, so anything that happened while you were reading it was not there — and the moment you are on that screen is usually the moment something is happening. Now it follows the log, and the text you were reading stays put while the new one is built.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_15_2
string-array.item: The marks that say where each trigger of a set stands are quieter now: a dot the size of a full stop, worn in the corner of the trigger\'s own icon, instead of a glyph at the end of the row. Filled and green where the rule is met — it has happened, or it is true at this moment — hollow where it is not, and hollow and faint where nobody can answer yet. Same meaning, a tenth of the noise.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_16_0
string-array.item: The card at the top is the soonest thing that *can* happen now, not the soonest thing with a date on it. Those were the same until a phone filled up with places: nothing waiting on an arrival has a date, so one appointment months away was winning the top of the screen — counting down 138 days — while five other reminders were going to ring that evening. A place with hours on it does have a floor, the moment its window opens, and now says so: «como pronto, 18:30». A place with no hours stays in «cuando ocurra», a random draw is never lifted out, and nothing more than a week away is lifted at all.

A fix that came out of the same report, and it was silently losing reminders: editing only the words of a reminder cleared the moment it was armed for without setting it again, and a firing with no armed moment is one the app drops. The alarm was still set; it just arrived to a reminder that no longer believed in it. The editor re-arms by hand now.

resources.string: How a full-screen reminder that keeps asking sounds: the same tone, round and round until you answer it. One asked for «sound» says it once and stops, on the screen as anywhere else. This preview stops itself after half a minute.

The phone\'s own alarm slider, here so a sound can be chosen at the level it will actually arrive at. Reminders play on the alarm stream, so this is the only volume that governs them — and at zero they are silent.
To the headphones when there are any

A reminder is an alarm, and an alarm comes out of the phone\'s speaker even with headphones on. With this on it goes to the headphones instead when a pair is connected, and whatever you were listening to drops a little and carries on underneath rather than stopping. Turn it off if your earbuds live in a drawer: a reminder played to nobody is a reminder missed.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_17_0
string-array.item: A reminder with sound now goes to your headphones when you are wearing any, instead of out of the phone\'s speaker as an alarm otherwise would. It is a setting, in Sound, and it is worth turning off if your earbuds live in a drawer: a reminder played to nobody is a reminder missed.

And it no longer stops your music. What was playing drops a few decibels and carries on underneath while the reminder sounds over it — the reminder is on the alarm channel and the music is not, so neither has to fight the other — and comes back by itself. It used to ask for the audio outright, which ended podcasts for a ten-second chime.

The Sound settings can now be listened to properly: the phone\'s alarm volume is a slider right there, so a sound can be chosen at the level it will actually arrive at; «Oírlo en continuo» plays it the way a full-screen reminder does, round and round (and stops itself after half a minute); and every one of those buttons turns into «Parar» while it is playing.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_123_0
string-array.item: The routines screen and its own rows now agree about contacts. The list is ordered by the turn each row shows — somebody whose cadence ran out is waiting their turn, not late — and the «overdue» chip is about having been told and left unanswered, so it can no longer hand you a list of contacts each reading «Yes».
A contact\'s turn is said as a day: «its turn on Friday afternoon» instead of «its turn in 6 d». The weekday inside the week, the date past it.

Settings says when there are more people than turns. One person of a kind comes up on each day you pick, so past that some of them would never come up at all — and the only sign was a row saying «no turn in the coming year». Now the row asks for attention and the card says the way out: another day, or cadences of about so many months. A kind with no day left says that too.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_122_0
string-array.item: «See» on a locked phone now asks to unlock first, and the reminder stays on the alert until that goes through. It used to take the alert away and leave you looking at the lock screen.

A «done» can be taken back from the two places that had no way back: the alert screen and the notification. It was a routine\'s alone; now it is any reminder, and the card carries the row it would put back — for ten minutes, after which «Hechos» is where an undo belongs.

The safety net\'s cards now say what they know and offer what they are for. One about a reminder that can never ring says so, and takes you to its form; one waiting at a place offers to lift the wait, which until now lived only in Home\'s long-press menu.

The backup says when it has stopped going through. A network failure is retried in silence, so changes could wait for weeks with nothing but a line inside a folded group to say so: now the row asks for attention, the disc on Home becomes a warning, and one quiet card says since when.
In a reminder\'s history, «not yet» no longer reads as «put off». Nothing was postponed, and the line said there was.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_121_0
string-array.item: When a new version has downloaded and is waiting to be installed, a small green arrow now sits on the cog beside the name on Home, and on the Updates row in Settings even while it is folded — so an update no longer waits unseen until you happen to open Settings.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_120_0
string-array.item: Contacts added in one go no longer all come due together. Until you first mark somebody «Spoken», their first turn is drawn anywhere inside their first cadence, so a batch typed in one evening starts coming up little by little from now, instead of all at once the day their cadence runs out.
And after every «Spoken», the cadence moves up to 10% either way, drawn again each time: the people you spoke to on the same day do not all come back on the same one.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_119_0
string-array.item: Adding a contact now asks for the name and nothing else. Kind and closeness are picked on the way in, and the cadence, days and window come from Settings, so the form opens with the keyboard ready and nothing more. Everything else is still there when you open the contact to change it by hand.
Fixed: a contact\'s row read «its turn in in 96 d».

string-array.name: whats_new_0_118_0
string-array.item: Keep in touch, refined. «New routine» now asks a step at a time: a routine or keep in touch; if keep in touch, work or personal; and whether it is somebody really close or somebody to keep up with now and then. The form opens with whatever Settings say for that pair.

By default, work contacts come up on Wednesdays 9:00–12:00, every 3 months when close and every 5 otherwise; personal ones on Fridays and Saturdays 17:00–19:00, every 2 months when close and every 5 otherwise. It all changes in Settings → Contacts, and the change reaches every contact you already have, except what you changed by hand on one: the form says what follows Settings and lets you go back to them. The contacts you already had are now close, and follow Settings.

How you are told: each window draws a moment, and at that moment the contact whose turn it is goes out — the close ones first, then whoever has gone longest without being told, and chance if they tie. At most one work and one personal contact a day; when their windows coincide, one of each, the first to whoever ranks first: a close friend, a close colleague, a sporadic friend, a sporadic colleague.

The card asks «Have you called Ana?», never makes a sound, and offers «Spoken» and «Put off a week». Left unanswered, it comes back the next day at the same time as a safety net, and that contact stays out of the draw until the week after.
Fixed: a contact\'s safety net made a sound, and every new contact got a «did not ring» card the day after it was written.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_117_0
string-array.item: Contacts: the people you would stop speaking to if nobody kept count.

Add someone with a cadence — «every 8 weeks» — and mark them work or personal. When the time is up, Rwilco tells you: a quiet card, never a sound, never taking the screen. Work contacts come up on a weekday morning, personal ones at the weekend, at a time drawn inside the window rather than on a clock.

And it paces you. Two work contacts and two personal ones a week at most, because that is how many slots there are — one person to a slot. Everybody else waits their turn, and the list says whose turn is when. A contact you do not answer comes back next week, ahead of the rest.
They live with the routines: same screen, same swipes, same «hecho». The slots and their hours are yours to change in Settings → Contacts, and that list is also the limit.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_116_0
string-array.item: A promotion to the stable channel now says its piece and stops. That channel moves in jumps of twenty or thirty releases at a time, and it was handing over every entry it jumped — each one written for the channel that tests the app, one per build. That is not a change log, it is a wall. The promotion\'s own summary is the whole of it now.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_115_0
string-array.item: It has been a while since the last update here, and a fair bit has piled up. The short version:

Routines are new — for the things you do every so often rather than at a set hour: watering the plants, changing the sheets. Rwilco keeps count of how long it has been, tells you on the main screen, and can ask you about it, either on the clock or when you get somewhere.

The rest, briefly: a reminder can now depend on the day of the month, or on whether you are walking or driving; alerts arrive more reliably; the app updates itself properly on a slow connection; and letting reminders through total silence can finally be switched on.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_114_0
string-array.item: Letting reminders through «total silence» can now actually be allowed.

Do Not Disturb lets alarms through in every mode but that one, and Settings has been offering «Ring even on total silence» — but the button opened the phone\'s list of apps allowed through, and Rwilco was not in it. Nothing you could do there, because an app only appears on that list if it says it wants to, and this one never did. It says so now, so the switch is there to turn on.
Until you turn it on nothing changes: the permission grants nothing by itself, and the alerts keep getting through every other Do Not Disturb mode the way they always have.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_113_0
string-array.item: The self-update now finishes on a bad connection, instead of spending data and never arriving.

The APK is sixty megabytes and each attempt gets ten minutes. On a slow network it did not fit — and every retry started at byte zero — so the five attempts spent up to three hundred megabytes of mobile data and installed nothing, with «download failed» for an explanation. Each attempt now asks for what is missing and adds it to what is already there, so the retries add up instead of repeating each other. If the server will not do that, it starts again; and if it turns out the file was already whole, it is taken as done rather than getting stuck asking for a piece that does not exist.

What is still arriving is no longer called the same as what is ready to install: it only takes that name once it is whole. So a cut-short download cannot be mistaken for an update ready to go, and a failed attempt does not leave sixty megabytes forgotten in the cache.

And choosing a channel in Settings checks there and then. It used to write the setting and nothing else: the answer arrived with the periodic check, up to twelve hours later, from a control you had just touched.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_112_0
string-array.item: «Y sólo si voy en coche» now says it with the words people use: on foot, in a vehicle, or either way.

There were two options — «en movimiento» and «en coche» — and the first did not mean what it looked like: it was a floor, so a car cleared it too. That is why it could not be called «andando» without lying. The condition has a ceiling as well as a floor now, and with it the three answers people actually want to give are all sayable: «andando» is moving but below the speed of a vehicle, «en coche» is from there up, and «cualquiera» is moving, either way. Anything already saved means exactly what it meant: an old «en movimiento» reads as «cualquiera».

And the choice goes away when «sólo al cruzar la línea» is off, where it meant nothing: a speed is a question about the instant of crossing, and «mientras esté en casa» has no such instant. It goes with «y quedarme allí un rato», which is there for the same reason. A speed set from «Sólo si» on a place read as a state stays put: the sheet does not put that question there, so it does not answer it either.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_111_0
string-array.item: A wake-up that did nothing, several times a day.

When a set with a deadline also has a firing the phone slept through, the deadline steps aside so the firing goes first — that is right and has not changed. What happened is that the deadline\'s alarm was set anyway, for a moment already behind the clock, so it arrived at once, stood aside for the same reason, and the next pass set it again. And there is a pass every time any reminder in the list changes. It is not set at all while a firing is owed now, and comes back by itself as soon as that firing is resolved.
That also closes the one exit in the firing machinery that did not re-arm what was left behind it: it could not, without biting its own tail. Now it can.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_110_0
string-array.item: «Y sólo si voy en coche»: the fence that told leaving home from popping out for bread, and that had been doing nothing since 0.101.0.

It was never checked. When something rang, the app asked that condition without looking at where the phone was, and with nobody to answer the answer was always yes — so the fence stopped nothing, whatever the words under it in the editor say. Where it landed worst was on routines: a place marked «this counts as done» was inverted end to end, since a speed nobody could read did stop it and a walking pace did not. Strolling past the car reset the count of «mover el coche», and the routine went quiet for three weeks. It is asked for real now, and about the moment the reminder is for: a nine o\'clock the phone slept through and catches up at noon is a question about nine.

And it was hidden. «Sólo si…» was grey text under the trigger, the one control in that row that did not look like one; it is a chip with a «+» now, like the conditions it adds and at a size a thumb is meant to hit. Better still, the speed is asked in the place sheet itself, beside the line it is about, the way «and once I have been there ten minutes» already was. Written there it turns up as a condition on the rule, which is where it is edited from afterwards.

«En marcha» becomes «en movimiento», and a line under the choice says what each one means. They are not two ways of getting about but two floors of the same thing: «en movimiento» is cleared by a walk, and by a bike and a car too; «en coche» is a speed no walk reaches. Calling it «andando» would have said something false.

Routines: pausing and resuming one you had never done yet wrote a «hecho» nobody gave. One with a start date lost its «aún no empieza» for good and began counting from a date that had not arrived; and its questions went quiet for a tenth of the span, which is the silence that follows a real «hecho». A pause still freezes the count exactly as before; what moves now is the start, which is what a routine that has not been done yet counts from.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_109_0
string-array.item: The other half of the round: the places where the app knew a reminder would not ring and said nothing about it, or said the opposite.

A reminder that cannot ring now says so, twice. There is a line in red over «Save» while you are writing it — «This will never ring» — and a row on its card afterwards, because the one arrangement the app can prove will fail was the one it said least about: it went to «Overdue» with nothing to explain itself, since a card there says when it should have rung and this one never had a moment to miss. The safety net has a word for it too, once, the day after.

And a real one behind that: a time range with hours on it never rang at all. «From 09:00 to 11:00, and only if it is between 10:00 and 12:00» opened at nine, was refused by its own condition, tried nine o\'clock the next day, and gave up — so a range with any hours on it was silently a reminder that could never ring, and the editor said so in as many words. It rings at ten, which is what it says. Two ranges under «at once» were the same silence, since that reading turns each into the other\'s condition.

«Rings tomorrow 04:00» was a promise the night could not keep. Between going to bed and getting up nothing makes a noise, whatever its tiles say — that is deliberate and has been since 0.63.0 — but the editor went on saying «Rings», and Settings said, in so many words, that a trigger with an hour of its own ignored all of it. The line now reads «silently, you\'ll be asleep», and the sentence in Settings says what actually happens. Your hours are still yours to move.

A new reminder makes a sound. It was a card and a buzz, which in a pocket is a reminder that did not happen; «Sound» is on from now on, one tap either way, and Settings still answers it once and for all. Reminders you have already written keep exactly what you gave them.

«This phone may not ring» now knows about places. The permission that silences a place reminder — location «all the time» — lived in a card in Settings, behind a fold, so the one thing that stops an arrival ringing was said nowhere anybody looks. It is the eighth thing the strip counts, and only on a phone that actually has a place to watch.

And where a place is being written, the editor asks for the right thing. It used to say «place reminders need location all the time» whatever was actually wrong — no permission at all, an approximate one, the phone\'s location switch off — and hand you the app\'s page in system settings. It now tells the four apart and asks for the one that is missing.

A second «when» stops meaning «at once» when «at once» would mean silence. Two moments never coincide and were already spared; two time ranges that do not overlap are not two moments, and quietly became a reminder that could never ring. The editor warned, and a default whose warning is the only thing between you and silence is a bad default.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_108_0
string-array.item: A round on the five places where the firing could fail and nobody would ever find out. Nothing about it is visible; all of it is about the difference between a reminder that goes quiet and a reminder that goes quiet without a trace.

An alarm is no longer set on a row that would not take it. The moment is written down first and the alarm set second, and when the writing failed the alarm went ahead anyway — which was the worst of both: the alarm arrived, found a row saying nothing was due, dropped itself as a stray, and the catch-up could not see it either, because that column is exactly what the catch-up reads. It now leaves the alarm unset and says so; the next pass — a save, a settings change, the six-hourly check — puts it back.

Three failures that used to happen in silence now reach the diagnostics report: a pass that could not read your reminders at all (it armed nothing and cancelled nothing, and the report showed an unbroken run with a hole in it), a card the phone refused to put in the shade, and a place crossing that was consumed on its way to ringing — the one that could never be reported again, because the watch had already written down which side of the line you were on.
A routine\'s repeated question is kept somewhere it cannot be lost to two things happening at once.

And the place watch has a second way back. Every look arms the next one, so a look the system refused to arm leaves the chain broken — and the only thing that could mend it was the alarm that was never set, which left the six-hourly check as the whole recovery. Opening the app now mends it too, and a watch with nothing left to look at no longer claims a look is coming.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_107_1
string-array.item: The routines\' polish round. «Yes» is a button with its word, not a bare tick, and it is not offered before a routine\'s count has begun. The snackbars and labels on that screen speak of a routine («Deleted», «Routine actions», «Clone routine»), Back closes the search and then the chip as it does on Home, and a routine found by Home\'s search says «Routine» in its own colour and opens the routines with it in view.

For a screen reader: a folded routine says its state («Yes · 1 d ago · due in 19 d»), an open one reads its question and answer as one sentence rather than an arrow, the pause control names the routine as its neighbours do, and Home\'s overdue row says its header first.
The span chips under a routine read as what they will be — «every day since the last time», not «the next day».

string-array.name: whats_new_0_107_0
string-array.item: «Sí» is a button. The answer to the card\'s own question was a swipe held, a held menu and a screen-reader action; it is the first control in the card\'s footer now, beside pause, edit and «⋯». A routine put off says «pospuesta» instead of «No» and carries the snooze under its count, and a paused one says «en pausa»: neither is something owed, so Home\'s line, the launcher and the «Overdue» chip leave them alone. Two chips more, «Paused» and «Not started yet», while any is.

Home\'s overdue rows answer like every card: a swipe held is «yes, done», the other way deletes. Three rows at most, and the rest counted in one; the count ticks by the minute; and when nothing is owed the door names the next one to run out («Regar las plantas · due in 3 d»). The widget\'s overdue number includes the routines owed, and the launcher keeps two slots for them so the pinned presets keep theirs.

A «done» given from the shade can be taken back: «yes, now» on a question and «done» on a ring leave a mute card with «undo», the way a place\'s own «done» does. The question cards join the app\'s bundle and wear the routines\' colour; «View» on a routine\'s ring and the tap on its question both land on the routines with that one in view, not on the form.

The routine\'s alert says its span where a rule\'s line used to name a question as the reason («its span: every 21 days since the last time»), heads its offers «not yet» — which is the honest answer at three in the morning — and puts «to a date» first, because ten minutes is no answer to a three-week span. The ring card in the shade says the span even with no rules.
A question dropped because you were not where the rule wants you («and only if I am at home») is asked again every quarter of an hour while its window is still open, instead of lost until tomorrow.

The form warns on a rule that is not a question under a routine (a date, a countdown, a draw: they ask once, or never); a preset kept from a routine no longer carries the day that routine began; and the history card under a routine drops the questions and opens with «done 7 times · every 23 d on average».

string-array.name: whats_new_0_106_0
string-array.item: A place that counts a routine as done no longer counts it again on its own. Written as «while I am outside the garage» (the reading 0.104.0 opened), the watch forgot which side you were on while the routine kept quiet after a «done», found you still outside when the quiet ended, and called that news — every tenth of the span, for ever, so the deadline never came. It remembers now: a place counts once when you come to its side (or are already there the first time it looks), and not again until you have left.

Pausing a routine freezes its count. The time it rests is not time that passed: a car a month in the shop still owes eleven days on the day the pause is lifted, not nineteen days ago and ringing that same second. The row keeps saying «hace 10 d» and «Sí» for as long as it rests.

«The last time was Monday.» The start chip on a routine takes a moment behind you as well as one ahead — it is the same anchor — and the line over «Guardar» says which. A routine written on Wednesday with the plants watered on Monday comes out with its count right.

A question the phone slept through is still asked. The next question used to be looked for from now, so a nine o\'clock the phone was off for was simply gone until tomorrow; it is looked for from the last one now, and a moment already gone is asked the moment the phone is back. Two doors within minutes are one question whichever put the first, and a routine just written — or told to start next month — is no longer mute for a tenth of its span from the day it was written: the quiet is what follows a «done», and only that.

Four things that could not happen through the form and could through a backup or an old preset, closed: a reminder turned into a routine sheds the ring it had already given (it used to never arm, never ask and never get the net\'s word); a routine put off «until I get home» keeps watching the places that count it as done; a stray repeat on a routine is no longer lifted into a calendar on read, taking the routine with it; and a routine never carries a set\'s deadline, whose lapse would have written a silent «done».

Smaller: «not yet» on a question leaves a line in the history; the undo of a place\'s «done» never moves the count forward past a later «done» of your own, and leaves its own line; the net\'s word on a routine keeps the question («ICYMI: Have you done…?»); and the diagnostics say when a routine will next ask, until when it keeps quiet, and when its deadline is.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_105_2
string-array.item: A folded routine that has run out says «No» at the end of its line, as the open one does. The colour says «look here»; the word says what it is. Only on a «No» — a column of «Sí»s down the right-hand side would be six answers to a question the folded shape does not ask.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_105_1
string-array.item: An overdue routine is now impossible to miss. Folded away it was a red hairline where the others had a pink one — the same shape, a different tint, at arm\'s length nothing at all. It is red from the edge in: the band, a wash under the whole card, and a track that is thicker than a hairline because folded away it is the only answer the card gives.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_105_0
string-array.item: The routines fold away. A button over «New routine» takes the whole list down to a line each — the words and the track of the plazo, no counts, no controls — and a tap on one opens it back out on its own. The same gesture and the same button Home already had, and what you choose is remembered.

And the screen has colour in it. Every card wears a band of the routines\' own colour down its leading edge, and the track runs in that colour while the plazo is still going and in red once it has run out — which is the one thing worth seeing without reading.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_104_1
string-array.item: The word «reminder» is gone from the routine form. The title said «New routine» and the card under it still said «Reminder · Write the reminder · What do you want to remember?», and so did the refusal when you left it blank and the delete button\'s label. They all say «routine» now, and the chip that reads a date out of your words — which would have written a trigger a routine has no use for — is not offered there.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_104_0
string-array.item: «Nueva rutina» now opens a form that calls itself that. It said «New reminder» — true of the model, since a routine is a reminder, and a lie about what you were writing. The title follows the thing being written, so a reminder turned into a routine by the chip is renamed there and then.

A routine can start later. The new «When it starts» card has two answers — «right now», which is what every routine did, and «at a future moment», off the same calendar «snooze to a date» uses — and reads the whole sentence back under them: «starts on 1 October, and then every 3 months since the last time». Nothing is owed until that moment arrives, and the list says «starts in 5 d» rather than counting time that has not passed.

«How often» is only the span now. It carried «every so often» and «since the last time», which on a routine were literally the same thing — both wrote the same span since the last time, from the same dialog — plus three answers («don\'t repeat», «specific days», «left to chance») that quietly stopped it being a routine at all. One chip, «another span», and the hour.

A routine offers the three triggers that can ask: a place, a time of day and a day of the week, each saying what it does there («asks at 09:00»). A date, a range, a countdown or a draw all name one moment and then have nothing more to say, which is a fine way to ring once and a poor way to ask a question that comes back every three weeks.

A routine\'s place counts if you are already there. It could only be written as a doorway — «on arriving», «on leaving» — so a phone that never crossed the line when it mattered was never asked at all. It now has the four readings it has on any reminder, and «while I am in the garage» counts from the first look that finds you there.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_103_0
string-array.item: A routine\'s safety net waits half an hour at the least. The word about a ring that got away comes a tenth of the way to the next one, which on a routine of one hour meant six minutes — the same reminder twice in the shade in six minutes, which is the nagging the net exists not to be. Long spans are unchanged: three weeks still gets its word a day later, and a routine still loses least by the silence, since its count is on its own screen and on the home row either way.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_102_0
string-array.item: The routines have a search. The magnifier in the bar opens the same field Home searches with, and the words narrow the list without re-ordering it: what is owed stays on top. It works alongside the chips — «Overdue» plus «filter» is what you would expect.

The cards are quieter. The count is in the muted ink whatever the answer is, and the span\'s track is a hairline. The «No» at the end of the question is what says the span has run out, and saying it three times on one card was twice too many.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_101_0
string-array.item: «And only if I am in the car». A rule can now be fenced to the speed the phone was going at — «Only if» → «Speed» — which is what tells leaving for the evening from walking to the bins, and what lets a routine that resets on the way out have a circle wide enough to actually be crossed.

It is worked out between two of the watch\'s looks, so it is not always answerable. When nothing can say, the reminder rings anyway — the same rule every fence here follows. The one exception is a place that counts a routine as done: that is the app acting on its own, so a speed it cannot check stops it rather than restarting a three-week count for nothing.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_100_0
string-array.item: An overdue routine is on the launcher icon. Hold the app icon: the routines whose span has run out take the first slots — ahead of the pinned presets, because a preset is something you go looking for and an overdue routine is something that has to find you — and a tap opens the routines with that one in view. It does not mark it done: a stray tap on a home screen should not move a three-week count.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_99_1
string-array.item: Bringing a reminder back from a pause asks for it again. «While I am at home» rings once and then keeps quiet until you deal with it — otherwise it would ring all evening — but a ring nobody answered was keeping it quiet for good: paused and resumed three days later, standing in the very place, nothing happened. Resuming now starts the round again. It still answers nothing, moves no anchor and finishes nothing; pausing writes nothing at all.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_99_0
string-array.item: A routine no longer rings like a reminder. The full screen lights up in the routines\' own colour and says ROUTINE where it used to say the app\'s name, and in the shade the card asks «Have you done “move the car”?» instead of repeating the words back at you.
Routine cards are reminder cards now: bigger, with pause, edit and «⋯» in plain sight rather than behind a long press only.
«Snooze» always ends with «to a date»: a calendar and an hour, for the answers that are a week away rather than ten minutes. On the routines, on Home, and on the alarm itself.
Home stops counting overdue routines in a box and gives each one its own row — its words, how long it has been — and a tap lands on that routine inside the list, ready to be dealt with.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_98_0
string-array.item: «And only on the 1st». A rule can now be fenced to days of the month, not just to days of the week: the 1st, the 15th, the last one. Pick them in «Only if» → «Month days», as many as you like.

Which is the only way a routine can ask its question on a date: its «Comes back» is already taken by the span, so «ask me on the 1st whether I have changed the filter» had nowhere to live. The 31st means the last day in a month that has no 31st — February included.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_97_1
string-array.item: Housekeeping, and nothing you can see: eight words and two functions the app no longer read anywhere are gone — what was left of the old «keep reminding me» switch, of the place picker before this one, and of a backup row that moved into its own screen.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_97_0
string-array.item: Your own tone and buzz stay where you put them. A routine\'s question, a word from the safety net or a ring could remake the notification channels for the *default* tone — which deletes the ones your chosen tone and rhythm ring, and puts them back at the next alarm. Now a card makes only the channel it is about to use, the whole set is rebuilt when you change the tone, and the insistent tone keeps its own channels instead of taking turns with the ordinary one.

Home\'s routines line says which one is overdue out loud. With TalkBack it read only «Open the routines»; now it reads the row as it is written — «You still haven\'t done: move the car» — and then where the tap goes.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_96_0
string-array.item: Routines ask. A time of day or a weekday under a routine puts a question in the shade — «Have I done “move the car”?» — with «Yes, just now» and «Not yet». Never a ring; the ring is still the deadline. A routine keeps quiet for a tenth of its span after you\'ve done it, and stops asking while its alarm is waiting for an answer.

A place can vouch for the deed. On a routine, a doorway is either «ask whether I\'ve done it» or «count as done, without asking»: leaving the garage is the car moving, so the count starts again by itself, a quiet notice says so with «Undo», and the history keeps the line. A place there is always a doorway, and the stay («and once I\'ve been out ten minutes») is the cheapest proof there is that you drove off.
Tapping a question opens the routines; «Done» anywhere answers it. A new channel, «Routine questions», carries them with the phone\'s own sound and goes silent in your quiet hours.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_95_0
string-array.item: Periodic routines: things you do every so often — move the car, water the plants — that count the time since the last time. «Comes back» has a new answer, «Since the last time»; a routine rings when that long has passed, and marking it done starts the count again from now, never from the one that was coming.

Their own screen, behind a line Home keeps under the chips: «You still haven\'t done: move the car» when one is overdue, quiet when none is. Every row is the question — «Have I done “move the car”? → Yes/No» — with how long it has been and how long is left. Swipe right and hold to say yes; swipe left to delete; tap to edit; filter by overdue or by tag.

Settings has «What a blank routine does», beside what a blank reminder does. Under a routine the form asks for what its rules will do — ask you whether you\'ve done it — and a place there is always a doorway; asking and counting a place as done arrive in the next release.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_94_0
string-array.item: An open card has a ⋯ beside its pencil: the same menu the long press opens — put off, skip the next one, clone, keep as a preset — behind a button you can see.

The form reads as one thing now: the words, then when, then «Comes back», and the tags after. Warnings under a rule are no longer amber (amber means what fires next); one that means the reminder will never ring is red. A counter appears as the words near their limit, forty for a preset\'s name. The form says when saving a finished reminder puts it back on the list.

To a screen reader: the big button on a ringing alert comes first, not after nine snooze offers; every screen\'s title is a heading; the pencils and bins on rules, phrases and recurrences say which one; the hero card says its tap opens the form; the card menu\'s backdrop says it closes; errors under a sheet are announced as they appear.

Settings: a group you open scrolls into view; closed rows keep two lines of summary at large text sizes; the Do Not Disturb offer is a row like its neighbours. The alert respects a punch-hole on a phone on its side. Every hand-rolled button buzzes like the rest.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_93_0
string-array.item: A silenced alarm stays silent when the phone is turned sideways. Rebuilding the screen used to start the alarm over for a fresh minute, red button and all.

A notification now opens its screen over the main list, whatever was open: Settings no longer lands on top of a half-written reminder, and a second backup notice no longer builds a stack of screens to walk back through. The watch\'s notices open the log they are about. And two quick taps on «New» open one form, not two.

Search starts at the top of its results, and closing it leaves the list where it was. Back clears a tag filter before it leaves the app. The tags panel has its door even when no open reminder wears a tag. The fold button no longer sits over the last card\'s controls.

«New» has a way back from the list of presets, and a «Close» on both steps. Deleting a reminder from the form gets the same minute-long undo row the list has. Renaming a tag says how many reminders it reached, with an undo.

Every sheet asks before a tap outside it throws your edit away — it was two of eleven. The list of trigger kinds scrolls, so «Place» and «At random» are reachable at large text sizes. A countdown reads «Rings tomorrow 09:00» rather than «Rings at tomorrow 09:00». A weekday sheet with no day marked, and a place with no pin, say so in red beside the greyed button. Cancelling a fresh trigger returns to the list of kinds. AM/PM buttons are a full thumb\'s height. The keyboard goes down before every sheet.

Settings: «Safety net» sits after «Vibration» as intended; the release notes row is called «What\'s new», like the sheet it opens. Done: the list respects the screen\'s edges on its side, and each «Bring back» names its reminder to a screen reader.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_92_0
string-array.item: What the alpha channel has been carrying since 0.88.0, now on beta. Nothing is new in this build itself — it is the same app the test channel has been running, published where everyone can get it. The entries below say what each of those changes was.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_91_0
string-array.item: Removing a tag now reaches your presets as well. A preset keeps tags of its own and puts them on every reminder made from it, so a tag deleted from every reminder and left in a preset was not really deleted — it came back the next time you used that shape. Renaming reaches them too, and merges rather than leaving the shape wearing the same tag twice.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_90_0
string-array.item: A tag you are offered is now a tag you can delete. A tag left only on reminders you have finished still showed up when picking tags, but was missing from the panel behind the + on the main screen — the one place that renames or removes one — so there was no way to get rid of it. The panel lists every tag that exists now, finished reminders included.
Those tags still get no chip on the main screen, because a filter that finds nothing is not a filter. The panel says which ones they are instead of leaving them looking broken.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_89_0
string-array.item: The update channel now says where you stand. Picking a channel with nothing published on it yet moved the control and changed nothing else on the screen, which looks exactly like a control that does not work — so it says that, and says the other three cases too: an update on its way, being on the newest build, and being ahead of the channel you chose.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_88_0
string-array.item: Two update channels, chosen in Settings → Updates. Beta is the tested one and where you already are; alpha is builds as they are written, which nobody else has run. Going to alpha happens at the next check; coming back waits for beta to catch up, because Android will not install an older version over a newer one — the screen says so before you choose and again while it is true.

A downloaded update is refused unless it is a build of the channel you follow. The check reads the version inside the APK rather than trusting the file that named it, so a mistake in a manifest cannot move this phone onto builds it never asked for.
And a word about what this app is, at launch. It is experimental software written for one person: press OK and it comes back next time, or turn it off for good.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_87_0
string-array.item: Tags are one row now when you write a reminder: a + that asks for a name, the ones you use most, and the dots for the rest. It used to be a button that unfolded into a field, a heading and a grid of chips, sitting between the words and the "when".

And they are administered in one place: the + at the end of the row of tags on the main screen. Rename one, remove one, put the ones you use at the front of the row, or write one down before the reminder that needs it. Renaming and removing reach every reminder carrying the tag; removing asks first.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_86_0
string-array.item: Home scrolls better with a lot of cards. The app\'s own code is now compiled ahead of time instead of being compiled by the phone while you scroll — which mattered here more than in most apps, because Rwilco updates itself every few days and every update threw that work away.

And the list reuses a card\'s slot for another card instead of rebuilding it from nothing. Measured: composing cards was the whole of what a frame spent on the processor; laying them out and drawing them barely registered.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_85_0
string-array.item: A place you asked about "when I get there" or "when I leave" can now ask for a while as well: "when I get home, and once I have been there 10 minutes". Crossing a line is the loudest thing a place can do and the least reliable — walking past a door, a trip to the bins — and this is the answer to that. Under "when I leave" it counts the other side, which is what tells going out from going out for the evening.

A position or two on the wrong side is forgiven; leaving for good is not, and then it waits for you to arrive again. It costs four wifi positions after an arrival, never the satellites, and the phone\'s own geofences time the same wait for free. With the battery low enough that Rwilco can barely look, it says so instead of going quiet.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_84_0
string-array.item: The search no longer answers a name with a coincidence. Typing "ramon" used to bring up a reminder about ping pong tables, because its letters happen to appear in that order somewhere in the sentence. Letters in order still find what they are for — "cmp" still finds "comprar pan" — but only when they start where a word does.
