string-array.name: whats_new_0_83_0
string-array.item: A set of triggers under "all of them" or "at once" can be given a time limit: hours of the day on the day the set is due, or so many minutes from the first one that happens. When it passes with something still missing, the reminder is let go without a sound — done, or on to its next round.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_82_0
string-array.item: Less battery for the same watching. A phone carried about the house within a couple of hundred metres of a place it is watching used to be read as approaching it, and looked every two minutes all evening — thirty times an hour. Moving is not approaching: what counts now is getting nearer the line, so an evening indoors backs off to a look every quarter of an hour, and the first step towards the place brings it straight back to two minutes.
A place you asked to be reminded on leaving is looked at every half hour at worst, never the hour it could drift to before.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_81_0
string-array.item: The warning about a circle finer than your positions now says what it actually means. It is about right now, not about the phone: it reads the looks of the last few hours, so it appears indoors on wifi and goes away in the street under the open sky — and it is worded as what it is, a reminder that may be slow to notice you arriving, not one that cannot. All of this is best effort: a better position, or the system\'s own geofences, can still ring it.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_80_0
string-array.item: «When I leave here» now draws the smallest circle your position can defend — twice its own accuracy, never under 100 m — instead of a flat 150. Under the open sky that is a hundred metres and walking home from the park next door rings it; indoors it grows with the doubt, so nothing is promised that the phone cannot see. The button says the size it would draw.

A reminder whose circle is smaller than what your phone can measure says so on its own card, in red, on the rule it belongs to. The warning used to live only where a radius is chosen, which reached the next place you wrote and none of the ones written months ago — and those are the ones quietly not ringing.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_79_0
string-array.item: «When I leave here» now says how far «here» reaches. It draws a fixed 150-metre circle around where you are standing, and leaving it takes that plus your phone\'s own doubt — a good two hundred metres of walking. Nothing said so, so a reminder put off in a park next door never rang, which is the app keeping a promise nobody could read.

The diagnostics report says how far the phone is from the middle of every circle it watches, beside which side of the line it thinks you are on. Those two numbers together are what explains a place reminder that did not ring.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_78_0
string-array.item: The diagnostics report answers the questions the last one could not. Every circle carries a short tag, so a rule, a watch line and a place\'s own state can be told to be about the same place or different ones; a new section lists the circles being watched, which side of each one the app thinks you are on and whether it can be judged at all; a dropped reminder says which condition dropped it instead of «conditions do not hold»; and a reminder the log talks about is never one of the ones cut from the list.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_77_0
string-array.item: The place sheet now says when a circle is smaller than what your phone can actually measure. Arriving somewhere takes a position at least as tight as the circle, so on a phone whose fixes come back at ±70 m — indoors, on wifi, which is exactly where a home circle is judged — a fifty-metre circle never sees you arrive and the reminder never rings. Under the radius, in red, with the number your own phone has been managing lately.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_76_0
string-array.item: The blue dot is back on the map, and on every opening of the place sheet — not only when adding a new place. It was a side effect of the pin: opening a place you had already saved drew the circle and nothing to measure it against, which is the one screen where «is this circle where I actually am?» is the whole question. It also draws the position the place watch already has while the phone is asked again, so there is a dot even where the system\'s own providers answer slowly.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_75_0
string-array.item: The safety net\'s quiet word now says so in the words themselves: «ICYMI: sacar la basura». Its card carries the reminder\'s own text on a silent channel, and in a full shade that looked exactly like the alarm it was about — the little line that said «puede que se te haya pasado» sits beside the app\'s name and is the first thing a narrow row drops. A reminder still waiting at a place is not marked: nothing has been missed there.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_74_0
string-array.item: A reminder that comes back now says when. Marking one done from the list has always spent just that round and armed the next — but a card whose rule reads «Mondays» went on saying exactly that, including the Monday it had just been dealt through, and nothing on screen showed that the swipe had done anything. The repeat row says «back Mon 14 Sept 08:00» while it rests, and the confirmation says it too instead of the bare «Done».
Holding to answer is 200 ms shorter everywhere: the alert screen\'s «Done» and its snoozes, a card\'s pause, and the hold that confirms a swipe.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_73_0
string-array.item: «Ver» on one of several reminders sharing the alert screen now gives that reminder the whole screen — its words at full size, every snooze, and «Hecho» where your thumb is — instead of handing you the edit form. Deal with it and you are back among the ones that are left, one fewer; the arrow at the top comes back without answering anything.

A reminder you have just written is landed on: Home goes to wherever the new card ended up and opens that one card, so you can read back what you wrote and reach the pencil if something is wrong. Editing an existing one still leaves the list exactly where you were reading.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_72_0
string-array.item: A place reminder that rings «on arrival» no longer loses its arrival to a vague position. The app needs a position at least as tight as the circle to say you have arrived, but it used to settle for a much vaguer one to decide you were already there — and «already there» is the answer that keeps a reminder quiet until you leave and come back. Now a circle a position cannot settle is left alone until one can.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_71_0
string-array.item: A tap on a reminder folds it away, and another opens it out again — the same gesture both ways, on every card in the list. It used to mean two different things depending on how tall the card already was, and one of them took you off the list and into the form.

The form is behind a pencil now, in the corner of an open card where the fold icon used to be, and in the footer of the glowing one. Leaving the list is something you ask for by name; everything else a card does can be undone by doing it again.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_70_0
string-array.item: Tags sit against the left margin again. A card with a single tag drew it adrift in the middle of the footer: the row that lays them out reported less width than it had been given, and Android centres whatever does not fill the space it was handed.
The alert screen\'s quiet moment is one second now, not two — long enough to outlast a thumb that was already on its way down. What guards every answer after that is still the finger kept on it.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_69_0
string-array.item: The polish round. The chip that reads a «when» out of your words now sits right under the words as you type them, not two cards down; the date sheet offers the next seven days by name beside «Today» and «Tomorrow»; the pinned-presets panel edits a preset too, so one list does it all; the big map has its own «my location» button.

Words settled: one verb for deleting a reminder, «Paused» as what just happened, «Close» on the dialogs that only close, «Cuando suena / Cuando lo marco hecho» on the «Vuelve» card, and the widget\'s description says what the widget does.

Smaller things you may notice: the header buttons and the two floating buttons buzz like everything else; section counts and the backup badge are set in the numbers\' typeface; the empty Home says how the swipes and the hold work; a search that hits its cap says so; the glowing card shows as many tags as fit and a mark for the rest; «Raise» for the alarm volume raises it itself; every (i) says which setting it is about; the calendar reads whole dates to a screen reader; two lists that ended flush now say they go on.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_68_0
string-array.item: The alert screen\'s two quiet seconds are only for a screen that took you by surprise. A reminder you opened yourself — from a card or a note — and the strips left after you answer one of several are ready to hold at once; «Close preview» in the editor is a plain tap again. While the count runs, the screen says «One moment…» and then, once, «Hold to answer», rather than a bare number.

«New» is no longer amber: amber means what fires next, and the hero\'s glow is the only amber left to look for. The card you just saved is marked even when it is the one at the top, and a screen reader gets «done» and «delete» on that card too.

Home says «Nothing for today» when there is nothing due and nothing missed. The magnifier opens on your tags instead of a blank page. A tag filter stays visible in the header while you scroll, with an × to clear it. The widget redraws when you fix a reminder\'s words and counts what is overdue.

«Done» and Home no longer sit on a loading screen for ever if the store cannot be read: they say so, with the diagnostics a tap away. The done list is grouped off the main thread and its «today» moves at midnight.

In the editor a refused save now goes to the card it is about and marks it. A sheet with real work in it — a place, a calendar — asks before the back gesture throws it away. The line under the form says what a span counted from «done» really does: «and so on until you do it · then it comes back every 4 years». A place reminder gets its «rings when you get to Casa» line. A preset saved says so and offers to pin it; the preset chooser says what each shape does instead of counting its triggers; a preset\'s name is capped where it is typed rather than cut on save. Renaming a phrase or tag opens ready to type. The countdown preview names the day. A place rule that still needs background location says so under the rule.

Settings: the ten checks are two groups now — what stops a reminder arriving (counted, red) and what only changes how it appears. Home\'s strip names the worst problem rather than a count. A fresh install hears one sentence from the app before Android\'s notification dialog. A sound file that cannot be copied says so. An update found in the background no longer drops the install dialog on top of what you are doing; the notification asks, and a tap picks the moment. An update the app is not allowed to install says so in the shade. The light theme\'s amber and outlines meet the contrast floor.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_67_0
string-array.item: A deleted reminder can be brought back for a whole minute. The «Undo» in the snackbar lasted four seconds and the next swipe replaced it, so a delete followed by a «done» on the card under it — which is how a list gets cleared — was gone for good. Now a row at the top of the list keeps the same undo for sixty seconds.
«Overdue» is in the order things were missed, oldest first, and each card says so: «Was due 3 h ago». It used to sort by the day you wrote them and look exactly like a future card.
The Home header keeps its search, history and diagnostics buttons at large font sizes; the name gives way instead of the buttons.
A stretch of dates in another year says the year, on the cards, in the sentence over «Save», in the «only if» fences and in the readable export.
When several reminders ring at once, «Done» on each strip is never squeezed out by long snooze labels: the offers wrap above it instead.
Expanded, a notification shows the reminder\'s words in full, with the reason under them. A long reminder could not be read from the shade at all.

A reminder channel you muted under a sound or rhythm you no longer use no longer keeps «this phone may not ring» on Home for ever: channels of old tones are swept away, and «Unmute» opens the muted channel\'s own page rather than the app\'s list.

The «fix» buttons in Settings can no longer crash the app on a phone without that settings page; they open the app\'s own page and say so. «Exclude» for battery optimisation asks with the one-tap dialog instead of dropping you on a list of every app.

In the editor, moving a series\' start past its end now drags the end along instead of letting you build something the save then refuses. A place without a name, a countdown of nought and a week with no day ticked each say why «Add» is grey. And a location permission refused twice now has a way through: a row with an «Settings» button, shown even once a pin is on the map.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_66_2
string-array.item: A day outside this year now says its year — «Tue 3 Sept 2030» — wherever the app reads a moment back to you: the «rings tomorrow · then…» line under the editor, the cards, the history. A reminder that comes back every four years read as «then Tue 3 Sept · then Sun 3 Sept», the same day twice with only the weekday to tell them apart.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_66_1
string-array.item: Answering the full-screen alert takes a shorter hold: seven tenths of a second instead of a full one — the same hold a card\'s «pause» already takes, so there is one length to learn. The two quiet seconds after the screen comes up are unchanged.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_66_0
string-array.item: The full-screen alert no longer takes a tap. For the first two seconds after it comes up nothing but Silence answers — a count at the top says so and the buttons stay dim — and after that «Done», every snooze and «View» answer only to a finger kept on them for a second: a ring at the top fills, a tick comes up, and the answer is given when you let go. Let go early and nothing happens. The screen that wakes you at three in the morning, or lights up under a hand reaching into a pocket, was the one screen in the app where a stray touch could file a reminder away for good.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_65_3
string-array.item: «New» asks «blank or from a preset» again whenever you have a preset, pinned or not. It had stopped asking once a preset was pinned, on the theory that the row above the list already answered — but that row is a shortcut to the presets on it, not the way to the rest.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_65_2
string-array.item: The line in the drawer reading «1 reminder» and nothing else is gone. It is the heading the app puts over a bundle of alerts, and while there is an alert under it the drawer draws the alert instead — so you only ever saw that line when it had nothing left to stand for. It was left behind when you dealt with a reminder: the two cards a reminder can have came down together and the heading was counted twice, once per card, against a list the system had not finished updating. Now it is counted once. Any line already stuck in your drawer is swept away the next time the app starts.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_65_1
string-array.item: Opening a reminder\'s notification no longer sets the alarm off again. The sound belongs to the moment it rang — the alert screen made it, or the notification did — and pulling the shade down half an hour later is you reading the card, not the moment coming round a second time. It was loudest on the cards that were meant to be quiet: one that never rang on time, or one that arrived silent because it was the middle of the night, would start buzzing the instant you touched it. The screen still opens, with the same answers on it; it just says nothing now.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_65_0
string-array.item: Home takes you to the card you just saved. Editing the words leaves a reminder where it was and the list rightly stays put; editing *when* it rings moves it — to another section, sometimes to the very bottom under «whenever» — and then keeping your place means looking at where it used to be. Now the list goes to it, and the card is lit for a moment so you can see which one moved. Only when it is not already on screen: a list that jumps when nothing has moved is worse than one that does not move at all.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_64_0
string-array.item: Home has a folded-away mode. The small button over «New» takes every card down to a line: the words, a row of small glyphs for what rings it and what it does, and the tags on the right with a mark when they do not all fit. Thirty cards at full height is a lot of scrolling to answer «what have I got on», and that question is about the list rather than about any one reminder.

Either card can still be opened out on its own. A tap on a folded card opens that one — the form is one tap further, from the card that is now open — and an open card has an icon in its corner that folds it back. The button over «New» is a clean sweep either way: it does not leave yesterday\'s exceptions behind.

What folding costs, said plainly: the rules keep their kind and lose their words, the marks that say where a rule stands go with them, and the pause control goes (holding the card still offers it). «Next up» is never folded — it is the one card the screen is about.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_63_0
string-array.item: The step that asks you to silence an alarm before it will take «Done» now only appears when there is still a noise going on: the buzzing, and the tone that keeps coming back. A plain «Sound» says its tone once and stops after a second or two, and the red button used to stand there for the rest of the minute holding «Done» out of reach in a silent room — a step you paid for and got nothing back from.

Every card about a reminder opens the alert screen now, the safety net\'s two notes included. «It never rang» used to open the form and «still waiting somewhere» used to open Home, because that screen only holds a reminder it is owed an answer for — so those two would have flashed and done nothing. Now the note says so and the screen holds it anyway, silently: it is a note about something that already got away, not an alarm. Taking a wait at a place back without answering is still on the card, held down.

The list you get from «From a preset» says that it goes on. Its rows and the dialog\'s height divided neatly, so the last one you could see ended flush with the bottom edge — nothing cut, nothing to scroll towards — and every preset below it was invisible. The edge is faded now and the next row is half-shown. The same edge was lying in the pinning panel and in the list of kept «Comes back» shapes, which could not even be scrolled past its cap.

The map shows where you are standing: the blue dot everyone already knows, with a slow, faint wave going out of it. Aiming a circle at a doorway is a question about the distance between two things — the pin and you — and only one of them was ever on the map.

The trigger sheets no longer bounce. A sheet already as far up as it goes had two things answering a swipe upwards with a spring, and neither of them had anywhere to go, so the gesture got two stretches, a rebound, and no information at all.

Touch targets that were under the 48dp floor are on it: the tag chips, the segmented choices, the kept «Comes back» shapes, the pinned presets, the list rows behind «…», and the hold-to-pause disc. The «×» that takes a «only if» fence off a rule was the worst of them — a bare 18dp glyph, a third of the floor, on a control that destroys something, a few millimetres from the one that edits it. The glyph is the same size; the thumb now has 48. And a day in the calendar is the whole cell rather than the circle drawn inside it.

«Tomorrow morning» in the editor is the hour your day starts at, which is what the setting says and what postponing to «tomorrow morning» has always used. It was nine o\'clock written into the code, so the two disagreed the moment you moved your morning.

«New» only asks whether you want a blank one or a preset while the answer is not already on the screen. It asked from the moment a single preset existed anywhere, so every blank reminder — most of them — paid a tap for ever. With presets pinned above the list they are one tap away already; with none pinned the question is still the only door to them, and it still opens.

Removing a trigger from the form can be undone. It was the one destructive act here without a way back, and its bin sits next to the pencil that edits — so a slip cost a place with its radius dragged, or a calendar with its end date, and the only way back was to build it again.
And «Comes back» says «optional», like the three cards around it. It was the only one that did not, which made it read as a question the form was waiting on.

The top row could get stuck off the screen. It travels by what the list scrolled — which is what keeps it glued to the cards — and a list already at the top scrolls nothing, so a row hidden up there had no gesture that could bring it back. Scrolling by hand never got you into that state; anything that jumped the list to the top did.

Nothing makes a noise while you are asleep. Between going to bed and getting up — your hours, in Settings → The day — every reminder and every word from the safety net arrives silent and still, whatever its own tiles say: a reminder asked for at three in the morning is still an alarm at three in the morning. The card, the screen and every answer on it are exactly where they were; only the sound and the buzz are gone, along with the coming back for more of them.

And a moment that fell while you were asleep stays quiet when you finally see it. A countdown that ran out at four, on a phone that was off until nine, used to ring over breakfast — which is the three-in-the-morning alarm arriving late rather than not arriving. It is shown, on the card and on Home; it is shown without a sound. «Test an alert» is the one exemption: if you are asking whether the noise works, the answer cannot be silence.

A full-screen alert no longer holds the screen awake. It used to pin the phone lit for the minute the noise lasted; the screen now comes up so you see the alert and goes off when your own timeout says so.

Editing a reminder keeps the snooze you had given it. It was dropped on every save, on the reasoning that editing re-decides when a reminder rings — true of a change to the rules, and false of fixing a word. What it cost, from a real phone: a reminder put off until the next evening was edited, lost the snooze, left the section it was sitting in for the very bottom of the list under «whenever», and read as rung-and-ignored again — so the safety net went off at ten to seven about an alert that had been answered the night before. A change to the rules, the reading or «Comes back» still drops it, because there the old answer really is meaningless.

A reminder that plays its tone once now gives the audio back the moment the tone ends. Ducking is not a volume this app sets — it is every other app being asked to drop a few decibels and stay there until we let go — and nothing here was watching a one-shot tone finish, so two seconds of chime kept your music or your podcast down for the rest of the minute the alert was up. In headphones that is most of what you notice.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_62_0
string-array.item: The safety net is heard now. Its word — «you may have let this one go» — plays your ordinary, non-insistent tone at half the volume an alarm gets: enough to notice, and saying in the only unit a sound has that it is not the alarm.

And it keeps to the hours you are up. Being mute was what let the net speak at any hour without anyone thinking about it; half an alarm at three in the morning is still an alarm at three in the morning, so outside your waking hours the card is posted exactly as silently as before. It is in the tray either way, and the net is about something that already got away.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_61_1
string-array.item: The review round on yesterday\'s five. «Exactly the span» said the rules stop deciding, and for a place among them that was not true: the circle was still watched, still registered, and an arrival still rang it. Now the span really does take over — the watch drops the circle, the fence is given back, and the arrival rings nothing.
And a rule nobody is asking any more no longer wears a mark saying it is not being met, which stated a promise as a fault.

Adding two triggers, removing both and adding two moments back could leave you with «at once» — which for two moments never rings — inherited from a choice the app had made, not you. It is not inherited any more.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_61_0
string-array.item: An alarm that is making a noise now asks to be silenced before it will take «Done». The big button turns red and says «Silence»: it stops the sound and the buzzing and nothing else, leaving the words, the snoozes and «View» exactly where they were to decide with — then it becomes the ordinary «Done». Half awake, «make it stop» and «I have done that» are the same reflex, and only one of them is true.

A reminder sent to your headphones comes out of the phone twenty seconds later if nobody answers. Bluetooth earbuds routinely hold two devices, and while the other one has the channel there is nothing to hear — with no sign of it from here.

«A day of the week» is its own trigger now. The days used to be welded to «Time of day», so saying just «Fridays» meant inventing an hour to say it with; write the two separately and they join with «at once», reading back as what you actually meant.

A second trigger now means «at once» rather than «either one» — one arrangement with two halves is almost always what a second «when» is for. Two triggers that can never coincide keep «either one», because «at once» there would be a reminder that never rings.

«Fridays at 14:00, and comes back every 30 days» stops being a guess. Thirty days after a Friday is a Sunday, and «Comes back» now asks which of the three you meant: the next allowed day (what it has always done, and it turns 30 days into 35), the closest one either side, or exactly the span whatever day that is.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_60_0
string-array.item: The top row gets out of the way. The wordmark, the cog and the icons slide away as you go down the list and come back the moment you go up — so Settings is a flick away from wherever you are reading, instead of a scroll back to the top. While you are searching the row stays put: the field is what your thumb is aiming at.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_59_0
string-array.item: The firing audit. Every way a reminder could stay quiet when it should have rung was hunted down, and the real ones were all at the places: an arrival minutes after another rule\'s ring now rings; a crossing reported in a busy moment can no longer be swallowed halfway; «al llegar a casa» said while the phone cannot tell where it stands now starts on the right side of the line; and the fences ask to be put back whenever Play Services left a doubt.

A ring put off until a place has a backstop now: if the crossing has not come in two days, one quiet note says it is still waiting — the safety net\'s own channel, once, opening Home where the wait can be taken back.

An exact alarm the system refuses at the last moment is set inexactly instead of not at all; and the clock is pinned further afield — put backwards with a snooze in flight, the southern hemisphere\'s daylight changes, a quarter-hour time zone.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_58_0
string-array.item: The review round. A reminder put off until a place could go quiet for good: the watch held its circle to the rule for a place that has already rung, and dropped the first arrival home. It rings now. And a second arrival in the same look, or a place snooze whose undo forgot which side of the line you were on, no longer gets lost.
A backup from a newer build restored here no longer wipes every setting over one word it does not know: the theme, the sound, the saved places and the presets each read what they can.

«Hecho» on a ring no longer forgets the rounds you had already skipped; the safety net\'s word gets a card of its own instead of replacing the alarm; a deleted reminder brought back keeps its history; the words «esta noche a las 9», «a las 12 de la noche» and «a la 1» read as anybody means them; and a repeat read from the words is offered under «Vuelve» even once a rule is on the form.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_57_0
string-array.item: Put off until a place. A ring can now be answered with «al llegar a Casa» — the saved place your reminders name most — or «al salir de aquí», a circle drawn around wherever you are at the tap. No clock is set: the place is the alarm, and it rings the moment you cross the line. On the ringing screen and in a held card\'s menu, in the place family\'s colour; only with location «all the time», since that is what keeps it.
«Al llegar a Casa» is not offered while you are already at home, and «al salir de aquí» says so when the phone cannot tell where here is, and writes nothing.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_56_0
string-array.item: The words say when. Write «sacar la basura mañana a las 9», «dentista el jueves 17:30», «en 20 min» or «pastillas cada martes a las 8» — in Spanish or English — and the first chip under «Cuándo» offers exactly that, with a quote mark on it so it reads as the sentence\'s own answer. One tap and it is set; the words stay as you typed them, and nothing is ever set without the tap. A line shared from another app gets the same reading.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_55_0
string-array.item: A home-screen widget: what fires next and when, how many are due today, and «Nuevo». Two cells wide it says the words and the moment; four, the count and the button beside them. Tapping the words opens that reminder. It is the app\'s dark card on whatever the launcher is, and it says «a las 18:30» rather than a countdown, because a widget redraws when it is told to, not every second.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_54_0
string-array.item: A reminder keeps its history: the last few times it rang, was answered, put off, skipped or caught by the safety net, on a card of its own in the form. «¿Sonó ayer?» had no answer anywhere a person could find — the row keeps one of each stamp and the diagnostics ring keeps a week of everything. It goes with the reminder and stays on this phone; the backup does not carry it.
The diagnostics report says the same, five deep per reminder, so a question about one ring no longer needs the whole log.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_53_0
string-array.item: The pinned presets are on the launcher icon. Hold it, «Comprar pan», and the reminder is written without the app in between — or its words are asked for, when the shape left them open, the same two doors the button on Home has.

The places\' geofences are no longer torn down and put back on every start of the process. The place watch\'s own alarm starts it every few minutes to an hour on a phone that kills it, and a crossing in the gap between the remove and the add was a crossing nobody saw. A sync now compares what it would register with what it last did and leaves Play Services alone when nothing changed; a reboot, an update or the six-hourly net still register afresh.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_52_0
string-array.item: The map in the place sheet takes a share of the screen instead of a fixed strip, and opens full screen from a button in its corner: room to pan out along a street and find the corner, with the radius under it and one way back.
«Guardar como lugar», on the place sheet: the place made for a rule kept by name, so the next rule that means it picks it off a chip. Saved places could only ever be made in Settings.
«Y sólo si estoy en casa» can be written without going to Settings first: the condition sheet offers the place kind always, and «Nuevo lugar» names one on the spot.
Several ringing at once: «Hecho con todos» (a hold — five reminders go on release) and «Posponer todos», under the strips.
Tap the month\'s name in any calendar to pick a month and a year; a date a year out was twelve swipes.
Export as text, from Backup: everything the phone holds, in its own sentences, readable by anything — and shareable. The vault is the copy that survives; this is the copy that can be looked at.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_51_0
string-array.item: These notes are back. The sheet had been silent since 0.20.0 — thirty versions with nothing said — and now a build cannot be cut without its line. Below this one, what happened in between.

«Saltar la próxima», in the menu of a card that comes back: one round let pass without pausing the reminder and remembering to come back. Underneath it is a «hecho» given early, which is what it always was; it just had no name.

Everything that can be deleted has a way back now: a preset, a saved place or window, a recurrence preset, a reminder brought back from the done list — each says so with an undo. Emptying a log asks first, and so does removing a tag from everything.
Search finds what was done too, after everything that is open and saying which it is. The history kept three months of it and the only way through was scrolling.
A filter that matches nothing says so, instead of a blank list under a lit chip.
A held stepper keeps counting, quicker as it goes. The step stays one minute — three minutes has to be sayable — and the long way round is no longer seventeen taps.
The three «when» chips everybody starts with — in half an hour, tonight, tomorrow morning — stay beside the ones learnt from your history instead of being replaced by them.
The card that glows has its own pause pill, like every other card.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_21_to_0_50
string-array.item: A place is a state, not only a doorway. «Mientras esté en casa» holds for as long as you are there; «al llegar» is the moment you cross the line. Under «todos», a place you have since left comes undone again, and a place that has rung is owed a leaving before it rings twice.

«A la vez»: every rule true at the same moment. «En casa, y de siete a nueve y media» rings the instant the last of them becomes true, and a doorway is a moment, so «al salir, y a la vez a las 13:30» no longer rings at 13:30.

«Vuelve» is the one place anything repeats: a calendar of its own, or a span counted from the ring or from the «hecho». A «hecho» does one round, and the next is the next. A calendar survives its first «hecho».

The safety net. A reminder that got away — the phone asleep, the alarm dropped — is caught within the hour and said quietly, with the word for what happened. Nothing to switch on; it is a tag nobody types.
«Posponer» from a held card, a snooze of your own length, «mañana por la mañana», and the two offers the notification shows are yours to choose in Settings.

The place watch: two eyes on every place — the phone\'s own geofences and the app\'s looks, paced by distance and speed, never a foreground service. Settings → Ubicación says what it last saw and when it looks again; the location log says it in sentences, and no longer prints an id where a name belongs.
The vault: an encrypted copy of everything in a private GitHub repository of yours, refreshed after every change, with export, import, a dry run and an undo.
The editor reads the reminder back in a sentence and says what will ring next; a refused save says why; an hour can be typed and stays in its half of the day.

A day without an hour is a stretch of it, not a lottery; a day can be counted instead of pointed at («en 3 días»); a preset for «mañana» means mañana every time; the calendar is a trigger too; a window says which days it allows.
Several ringing together stack in strips; the shade says why it went off; Home says when the phone may not ring, offers a rehearsal, and can be told «ahora no».

string-array.name: whats_new_0_20_0
string-array.item: «Vuelve» asks the whole question now. «Cada semana» was only ever half a sentence — the other half is which moment the week is counted from — and the app used to decide it silently: from dealing with it if you set a span, from the calendar if you happened to add a repeating trigger, and nothing on either screen said which one you had. Three answers, one row: the calendar, the ringing, or dealing with it.

«When it rings» is new, and it is the one people kept meaning. If the eight o\'clock dose is marked done at half nine, the next one used to be half three and the rhythm drifted later every day; counted from the ringing it stays at two. Worth knowing before you pick it: one left unanswered comes back on its rhythm rather than waiting to be acknowledged.

A recurrence can be counted in years. And a yearly repeat can name a weekday of its month, which nothing could say before: «el primer miércoles de mayo» is a real yearly, and every other way of writing it is arithmetic on a date that moves — the first Wednesday of May is the 6th in 2026 and the 5th in 2027.

The «add trigger» sheet is six uniform rows instead of a two-column grid. Six things in two columns is a shape that has to be read — across, then down, then back — and with an odd count the last cell is a hole.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_19_3
string-array.item: A set read as «todos» no longer watches its places around the clock. «El 26 de cada mes, y cuando llegue a casa» was spending a fix every half hour, every day, for a month — because under «todos» the siblings are rules of their own rather than conditions, so nothing gated the circle at all. It now waits for the run-up to the soonest sibling moment, like every other gated circle.

Nothing is lost by waiting. Under «todos» a crossing before the moment has to be written down, not caught in the act — the ring waits for the moment either way — and the phone\'s own geofences record it for free. And when the moment has already happened and the place is all that is left, it is watched at once: then it is the one that rings.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_19_2
string-array.item: A reminder that has been dealt with and is coming back on a span no longer puts marks on its rules. It is not waiting for them — it is waiting for the span, which the recurrence row already says — so a tick or a ring there was an answer to a question nobody had put.

The place marks were the worse half of it. The watch keeps a resting circle\'s last judgement on purpose, because a place that has rung is owed a leaving before it rings again; the card was reading that bookkeeping as a live verdict and saying «no se cumple ahora mismo» about a circle nothing had looked at in hours.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_19_1
string-array.item: Fixed, and a card was stating it with a straight face: a place under «a la vez» whose hours had closed kept showing the last thing the watch saw as if it were now. At eight on a Thursday morning, «al llegar a casa, entre las 19:00 y las 21:30» said «no se cumple ahora mismo» about a circle nothing had looked at since the night before. It now wears the mark that means nobody has looked, which is the truth.

The watch starts two hours before a window opens rather than at the stroke of it. Beginning at 19:00 meant the first fix went on learning which side of the line the phone was on, so somebody who walked in at 19:01 had arrived nowhere and was not rung. Two hours is enough of a run-up for an arrival to be an arrival — and a window once a day still costs two hours of looking instead of twenty-four, which is the whole point of leaving a circle alone.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_19_0
string-array.item: Settings is an index now, not a scroll. What was thirty-odd controls in one column — twice what any published guideline allows on a settings screen — is ten rows, each carrying its own current value: the sound by name, the hours you are up as «08:00–23:30», how many places you have kept. Most questions are answered without opening anything.

Each row opens where it stands, and they are independent: opening one does not close another and pull the screen out from under your thumb. A caret means «this opens here»; an arrow means «this goes somewhere else». Everything starts closed.

The groups are by meaning rather than by what happened to be next to what. «Reminders» was a drawer holding the default hour, the favourite trigger, the shape of your week and the vibration of the interface; it is now «New reminders» and «Your day», and touch feedback has gone where it belongs, with the theme. Location and Places were two sections saying the same thing and are one.

A fold is never allowed to hide a phone that will not ring. When something is in the way of a reminder arriving, the closed row says so — «3 cosas por arreglar», in red, with the badge to match — and that group opens itself the first time you come in. It is the only thing on the screen that moves by itself, and the reason is that every one of those failures is silent.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_18_2
string-array.item: Fixed, and it was silencing reminders: a recurrence counted in days ended its rest at the hour «the next day» starts at — nine in the morning by default — and that hour then stood in front of every rule due earlier. «When I get to work, between seven and eight, the next day» came back each morning to a window that had closed an hour before the reminder was allowed to look, so it never rang again. The plainest shape had it too: «every day at nine», with a day that starts at nine, rang every other day.

A recurrence now says which day it comes back on and the rules say when in that day, which is what the two were always meant to mean. A reminder that is only a place still waits for the day to start — there is no hour of its own to defer to, and without it «the next day» would begin one minute past midnight.

The mark for a rule nobody has been able to check yet — a place with no fix behind it — is a pause now, where it was a ring with a dot in it. Two bars are the one shape on a card that says «waiting» without saying yes or no, and being the odd shape out among four circles is the point: it is the odd state out.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_18_1
string-array.item: Using a pinned shape that asks for its words now shows what it will do when it rings, as five glyphs under the field: the shape’s own answer, already on, and a tap away from being changed for this one reminder. Asking for the screen just this once, or for silence just this once, no longer means editing the shape and putting it back afterwards. The shape itself is untouched.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_18_0
string-array.item: A date is one tile now, not two. Pick a day and the hour is already filled in with your usual one, ready to be changed — or hand the hour over entirely with «at random during the day», and the reminder lands somewhere inside the hours you are actually up.

Which the app now knows: Settings asks when you get up and when you go to bed, once for weekdays and once for weekends, and when the weekend ends as well as when it starts. So a Friday gets up for work and goes to bed at the weekend, and a Sunday keeps the lie-in and loses the late night. A trigger given an hour of its own ignores all of it.

«A repeating time» has grown into a proper recurrence: every so many days, weeks, months or years — the days of the week for a weekly one, «day 26» or «the fourth Wednesday» for a monthly one — starting on a day you pick and ending never, on a date, or after so many times. Its hour can be left to the day too.

Nothing skips. A monthly «day 31» rings on the 28th in February rather than not at all, a yearly 29 February rings on the 28th, and the ordinals stop at «fourth» and «last» because every month has one of those.

Fixed: opening «new tag» in the editor could take the Save button away for good — the field stayed open behind you with nothing to close it, and the button steps aside while it is open. It does not step aside any more, and the field closes when you move on.

Fixed: the chimes ended with a click. They were still at three to eight per cent of their volume on the last sample and then stopped dead; they now fade to a true silence. «Soft» is where it was most audible.

Fixed: the backup badge flashed a red nought as it left. And the highlighted card at the top of Home now lists its triggers and their marks, like every other card, which is where you most want to see which of them already holds.

string-array.name: whats_new_0_17_1
string-array.item: The little marks on a set\'s triggers are bigger and brighter, which they needed to be on the dark scheme: a third wider, a line twice as thick, and a solid middle so the ring keeps its edge over the coloured icon underneath instead of showing it through. The one that means «not known yet» is a ring with a dot in the middle of it now — it was a question mark, and a question mark three millimetres across is a smudge.

resources.string: On its own it rings at your usual time on the first day, and on each day it is still open until you deal with it.
With «at once» this is the stretch of the calendar the others have to fall inside: «at home, and between the 1st and the 15th».
Rings when the window opens, and goes on counting until it closes.

At most one a day of each kind, at a random moment inside the window, and never with a sound. What you change here applies to every contact, the ones you already have included, except what you changed by hand on one.

One person of this kind comes up on each day you pick, so %1$d people need more room than these days give — some of them would never come up at all. Add a day, or put their cadences at about every %2$d months.
No day picked: nobody of this kind will ever come up.
Stretches of the day kept by name, offered wherever one is asked for: at lunchtime, in the evening.
Rings as soon as your day starts, at %1$s, and goes on counting until %2$s. You set your hours in Settings.
What “at random during the day” draws from — and the hours anything is allowed to make a noise in. A trigger with an hour of its own still rings at that hour; outside these, it arrives silent.
From this moment the weekday bedtime applies again, which is what makes a Sunday night an early one.

Only what happens between these hours counts, on the day the set is due. If they close with something still missing, the reminder is let go without a sound — or waits for its next round, if it comes back.

The clock starts with the first thing that happens at a moment: an hour, a date, walking through a door. Not with a place you are already at. If it runs out with something still missing, the reminder is let go without a sound — or waits for its next round, if it comes back.
The clock starts with the first
